newsitem.title: UK: London gold turns quiet, enters no-man's land.
newsitem.headline: London gold turns quiet, enters no-man's land.

text.p: Precious metals prices were in "no-man's land" on Monday since firming towards the end of last week and needed another move before a direction would become apparent, dealers said.
"We are in no-man's land around $351-$353... People are keeping a watching brief on currencies and the (U.S.) stock exchange now that some of the steam has come out of," a dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $352.45 per ounce against $353.30 on Friday as it continued an almost unbroken series of rises since it fixed at a 3-3/4 year low of $336.90 on February 12.
Physical demand for gold remained significantly good even after the recent steady climb in prices, dealers said.

Premiums were being charged for ten-tola bars and kilobars, the standard investment sizes in Middle and Far East markets, and European refiners were quoting delivery times of around six weeks for recasting good delivery gold into these shapes compared with a matter of days normally.
Dealers also noted currency-related buying from Japan earlier encouraged by the weaker yen.
"There are arguments for gold moving in either direction from here," a dealer said, adding that the latest move to a band of $348-$354 had caught some market players off balance.
However the rise may have postponed some producer sales, dealers said.
"There could be a couple of sell orders taken out when the price popped up above $347.00 last week," one said, adding that if the price started to fall, then selling could accelerate.
Silver was quiet at an unchanged $5.22/$5.24, having profited from trading against the gold-silver ratio last week.
Dealers said physical interest remained high but ratio trading was quieter today after profit-taking on Friday.
Platinum and palladium were both firmer with the former fixing at $371.00, its highest fixing since December 27, 1996.
It was indicated at $371.25/$372.25, up $2.25, while palladium was indicated at $138.00/$139.00, having been fixed up $2.25 at $138.25.
Even so, dealers said there had been some profit-taking selling of the platinum group metals.

"There is still a lot of confusion over what will happen with the Russians and shipments to Japan," one dealer said, noting that a Russian export agency official was reported saying he thought exports to Japan would be much lower this year than last. --Brian Spoors, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8058
